title: Stroopwafels (Syrup Waffle Cookies)
summary: Thin, cinnamon-spiced waffle biscuits pressed in an iron and sandwiched together with a warm, chewy syrup filling while still hot.
equipment: stroopwafel iron, waffle-cone iron or pizzelle iron (essential)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt

steps.title: Activate the yeast
steps.text: Stir the fast-action dried yeast into the lukewarm milk and leave to rest for 5 minutes, until foamy. This confirms the yeast is active before it goes into the dough.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, caster sugar, cinnamon and salt, then rub in the butter until the mixture looks like crumbs. Add the egg and the yeasty milk, then knead briefly to a soft, smooth dough.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.text: Cover and rest the dough for 45 minutes at room temperature. The yeast here is mainly for flavour and tenderness rather than a big rise, so don't expect it to double in size.

steps.title: Cook the syrup filling
steps.text: In a small heavy saucepan over medium heat, stir the dark brown soft sugar, golden syrup, butter and cinnamon until melted. Boil without stirring to 112-115°C, the soft-ball stage, which takes about 3-5 minutes and gives the filling its chewy set. Sugar syrup at this temperature burns badly, so keep children away and never touch or taste it hot.

steps.title: Cool the filling
steps.text: Leave the syrup to cool for 5-10 minutes until thick but still spreadable, rewarming gently if it stiffens too much. A filling that's too thin will run out of the biscuits, while one that's too stiff won't spread evenly.

steps.title: Heat the iron
steps.text: Heat the stroopwafel iron on medium-high for at least 10 minutes before you start cooking. An iron that isn't fully hot will stick and won't crisp the dough properly.

steps.title: Divide the dough
steps.text: Divide the dough into 12 balls, each about 40g. Weighing them keeps every stroopwafel the same size, so they all cook in the same time.

steps.title: Press and cook
steps.text: Press one ball of dough in the hot iron for 1-2 minutes, until evenly golden and crisp all over. A good even gold colour across the whole waffle shows it's cooked through, not just browned at the pressure points.

steps.title: Split and fill while hot
steps.text: Immediately cut a 10cm round from the hot waffle and, while it is still hot and pliable, split it horizontally into two thin discs using the serrated knife. Spread 1 tablespoon of warm filling over one cut side, top with the other disc and press together, working quickly before the waffle cools and turns too brittle to cut.

steps.title: Repeat and cool
steps.text: Repeat with the remaining dough and filling, cooling each finished stroopwafel on a wire rack. Rewarm the filling between batches if it starts to set.

tips: Use a sugar thermometer for the syrup - a common mistake is guessing the soft-ball stage, which leaves the filling either too runny or too hard once cooled.
Cut and split each waffle the moment it comes off the iron, while it's still hot and flexible, as it turns brittle and hard to cut within moments of cooling.
Keep the filling gently warm throughout, as it firms up quickly and becomes difficult to spread if left to sit.
Weigh out the dough balls rather than eyeing them up, so every stroopwafel presses to the same thickness.
If your iron browns unevenly, rotate or adjust pressure slightly between batches rather than extending the cooking time, which can scorch the edges.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 4 days; warm briefly in a low oven or over a hot drink to soften before serving. They are not suitable for freezing once filled, as the syrup filling becomes very hard.
